issues.legal_issue: A lessee of land held as an intermediary’s grove does not retain an interest in the land after the statutory vesting when the governing scheme settles the land with the intermediary and grants no new right to the lessee.
material_facts: The disputed grove was held as an intermediary’s grove immediately before vesting.
The claimant held the grove land under leases from co-sharers but was not an intermediary within the statutory definition.
The governing land-reform scheme settled the grove with the intermediaries and provided no interest in the grove land to the claimant as lessee.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had no subsisting interest in the grove land after the Act commenced.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18(1), 2(12) and 2(13) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, land held as an intermediary’s grove immediately before vesting is deemed settled with the intermediary; a lessee who is not an intermediary acquires no interest in that land under the Act. The Act creates new rights in place of the old rights, which cease on its commencement. Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd. and Jamshed Jahan Begam v. Lakhan Lal were relied on. The Act, rather than the Transfer of Property Act, governs land covered by it.

rule.if: appeal_about_a_lessee_interest_in_land and land_was_an_intermediary_grove and claimant_was_a_lessee_not_an_intermediary and governing_scheme_settled_land_with_intermediary_and_granted_no_new_right_to_lessee

predicates.appeal_about_a_lessee_interest_in_land: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether a lessee retains an interest in land.
predicates.land_was_an_intermediary_grove: The land was held as an intermediary’s grove at the relevant time before vesting.
predicates.claimant_was_a_lessee_not_an_intermediar: The claimant held the land under a lease and did not belong to the class of persons treated as intermediaries.
predicates.governing_scheme_settled_land_with_inter: The governing scheme settled the land with the intermediary and granted no new interest in it to the lessee.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a lessee’s interest in land that was an intermediary’s grove, the claimant was only a lessee, and the governing scheme settled the land with the intermediary without granting the lessee a new right, the lessee has no subsisting interest in the land.

issues.legal_issue: A decision in an earlier proceeding does not operate as res judicata on an issue that was different from the issue decided in the later proceeding.
material_facts: A prior appeal arose from a suit seeking cancellation of the leases on the ground that they were invalid under a tenancy-law provision.
The question whether the land-reform scheme gave the claimant rights in the grove land was neither considered nor required to be considered in the prior appeal.
The present appeal concerned whether the claimant retained rights in the grove land after the land-reform scheme took effect.
issues.conclusion: The decision in the earlier appeal did not operate as res judicata in the present appeal because the issues in the two appeals were different.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata does not apply where the material issue decided in the earlier proceeding differs from the issue in the later proceeding. The earlier appeal concerned whether the leases were void; the present appeal concerned whether the land-reform scheme left the lessee with a subsisting right in the land.

predicates.appeal_with_res_judicata_claim: The proceeding is an appeal in which a party claims that an earlier decision bars the issue before the court.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_decided_a_different_m: The earlier proceeding decided a material issue different from the issue raised in the current proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal raises a res judicata claim but the earlier proceeding decided a different material issue, the earlier decision does not bar the current issue.
